seo.title: Best Vegan Cafes in Bali (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Bali's top 12 vegan cafes for 2026! From vibrant smoothie bowls to gourmet plant-based dinners, find the best spots in Ubud, Canggu, and Seminyak for delicious, ethical eats.

hero.subtitle: Bali is a global mecca for plant-based eating, boasting an incredible array of vegan cafes that cater to every taste, from healthy raw food havens to indulgent comfort food spots.

picks.name: KYND Community
picks.whyItMadeTheList: KYND Community is arguably Bali's most Instagrammable vegan cafe, famous for its vibrant pink walls and beautifully plated dishes. They excel in vegan comfort food and wholesome options, from loaded smoothie bowls to delicious plant-based burgers and curries. The atmosphere is consistently buzzing and friendly, perfect for a sunny Bali day.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Say Cheese' Burger and the iconic 'Tropical Paradise' smoothie bowl, personalized with your name.
picks.insiderTip: Go early for breakfast to snag a prime spot for photos and beat the mid-morning rush.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, KYND Community is worth the hype. Their vegan 'chicken' parm is shockingly good, and every corner is a photo op. Don't miss it if you're in Seminyak!"

picks.name: Alchemy Bali
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As Bali's original 100% raw vegan cafe, Alchemy is a beloved institution in Ubud. It features an extensive salad bar where you can build your own creations, alongside delicious raw pizzas, desserts, and potent elixirs. The cafe offers a tranquil, earthy vibe, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods for ultimate nourishment.
picks.whatToOrder: A custom salad bowl from their abundant salad bar, or a slice of their famous raw vegan cheesecake.
picks.insiderTip: Try their homemade kombucha on tap – they often have unique seasonal flavors.
picks.redditQuote: "Alchemy in Ubud changed my life! The raw vegan lasagna sounds weird but it's incredible, and their smoothie bowls are next level. Such a peaceful spot."

picks.name: The Shady Shack
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A Canggu favorite, The Shady Shack is a vibrant, laid-back cafe with a largely vegetarian menu that has extensive vegan options clearly marked. Known for its generous portions and creative dishes like the 'Halli-Mani' burger and 'Nori Bowls,' it's perfect for a casual lunch or brunch. The garden setting is incredibly charming and relaxed.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Crumbed Halloumi Burger' (ask for vegan cheese if available, or omit) or the 'Nori Bowl' with tempeh.
picks.insiderTip: It can get very busy, especially during lunch, so be prepared for a short wait or arrive slightly before peak hours.
picks.redditQuote: "The Shady Shack is my go-to in Canggu for a filling vegan meal. Their tempeh nori bowl is legendary, and the vibe is just so chill. Highly recommend!"

picks.name: Moksa Plant-based Cuisine & Permaculture
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Moksa offers a sophisticated farm-to-table experience with innovative plant-based dishes crafted from ingredients grown in their own permaculture garden. It's an immersive culinary journey that elevates vegan dining, blending Balinese flavors with international techniques. The serene outdoor setting, often accompanied by live music, makes it an ideal spot for a special meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Their signature 'Jackfruit Rendang' or the 'Mushroom Scallop' starter. Don't skip the tasting menu if available.
picks.insiderTip: They offer cooking classes focusing on plant-based Balinese cuisine; book in advance if you're interested.
picks.redditQuote: "Moksa is a must-do in Ubud for a special vegan dinner. The ambiance, the farm-fresh ingredients, the creativity in their dishes... it's truly an experience, not just a meal."

picks.name: Give Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Give Cafe is a feel-good spot that serves delicious plant-based Indonesian classics and western favorites, with 100% of its profits going back to local charities. The vibrant, colorful interior reflects its cheerful mission. It's a fantastic place to enjoy a budget-friendly, hearty vegan meal while supporting the local community.
picks.whatToOrder: The Nasi Campur, a traditional Indonesian mixed rice platter, allows you to pick your favorite vegan toppings.
picks.insiderTip: Check their Instagram for updates on which charity they are currently supporting.
picks.redditQuote: "You HAVE to go to Give Cafe! The food is amazing, especially their Nasi Campur, and knowing your money goes to charity just makes it taste even better. Total win-win."

picks.name: Zest Ubud
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Perched on a hillside overlooking the Campuhan Ridge, Zest Ubud offers an unparalleled dining experience with its stunning views and innovative plant-based menu. Their dishes are creative and comforting, ranging from vegan pizzas and pastas to unique breakfast bowls, all served in a beautifully designed, open-air space that feels deeply connected to nature.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Dragon Bowl' for breakfast or their vegan 'Meat Lover's' pizza.
picks.insiderTip: Aim to visit around sunset for spectacular views over the jungle and rice paddies.
picks.redditQuote: "Zest Ubud has the best vibes and views in town, hands down. Their vegan food is surprisingly hearty and creative. Perfect for a chill evening with friends."

picks.name: Peloton Supershop
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Doubling as a cafe and a bike repair shop, Peloton Supershop brings a cool, industrial-chic vibe to Canggu's vegan scene. They specialize in hearty, wholesome vegan meals like burgers, wraps, and their famous 'Tricken Schnitzel'. It's a popular spot for breakfast, lunch, and grabbing a coffee, attracting both locals and tourists.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Tricken Schnitzel Burger' is a must-try for vegan comfort food lovers.
picks.insiderTip: They often have unique seasonal specials, so check their blackboard for daily offerings.
picks.redditQuote: "Peloton's 'Tricken Schnitzel' is a revelation, seriously good vegan fried 'chicken'! Plus, their coffee is on point. Great place to refuel after a surf or bike ride."

picks.name: Sayuri Healing Food
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sayuri Healing Food is a nurturing space dedicated to raw and living foods, macrobiotic cuisine, and holistic wellness. It offers a diverse menu of delicious and nourishing dishes, from raw sushi to elaborate main courses and an impressive array of guilt-free desserts. The atmosphere is calm and inviting, with a strong focus on education and community.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Raw Vegan Sushi' platter or their famous 'Chocolate Avocado Mousse'.
picks.insiderTip: They run regular raw food workshops and community events; check their schedule if you're interested in learning.
picks.redditQuote: "Sayuri is my happy place in Ubud. Their raw vegan pizza is surprisingly satisfying, and their desserts are out of this world. Everything feels so wholesome and healing."

picks.name: Plant Cartel
picks.whyItMadeTheList: If you're craving indulgent vegan comfort food, Plant Cartel is your spot. This modern, stylish cafe in Seminyak specializes in plant-based burgers, loaded fries, 'chicken' wings, and decadent milkshakes. It's the perfect place to satisfy those junk food cravings with ethical, delicious alternatives in a fun, casual setting.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Classic Cartel Burger' with a side of loaded fries and a 'Strawberry Dream' milkshake.
picks.insiderTip: They offer delivery services, perfect for a cozy night in after a long day of exploring.
picks.redditQuote: "OMG, Plant Cartel's vegan burgers are legit. I swear they nailed the texture and flavor. My non-vegan friends were even impressed. Get the loaded fries!"

picks.name: Gora's Vegan Kitchen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Gora's Vegan Kitchen offers authentic, delicious, and incredibly affordable Indonesian vegan cuisine in a cozy, unpretentious setting. Located slightly off the main Canggu drag in Pererenan, it's a hidden gem favored by locals and savvy travelers alike for its flavorful Nasi Campur, gado-gado, and other traditional dishes, all made plant-based.
picks.whatToOrder: Their daily Nasi Campur is fantastic value, allowing you to sample various Indonesian vegan dishes.
picks.insiderTip: It's a small place, so it can fill up quickly during peak lunch and dinner times.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want amazing, cheap vegan Indonesian food, you HAVE to go to Gora's. Best vegan Nasi Campur I had in Bali, hands down. So fresh and flavorful."

picks.name: Living Food Lab
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Living Food Lab focuses on innovative raw and cooked plant-based cuisine, with a strong emphasis on fermented foods and superfoods. Their menu features vibrant bowls, wholesome wraps, and creative mains, all designed to be both delicious and incredibly nourishing. The cafe itself is bright and airy, with a community-focused vibe.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Kimchi Bowl' or one of their nutrient-dense smoothies.
picks.insiderTip: They also sell a range of homemade fermented products like kimchi and tempeh, perfect for taking home.
picks.redditQuote: "Living Food Lab is a fantastic spot in Canggu for healthy vegan options. Their kimchi bowl is addictive, and I love that they use so many fermented foods. Great energy there."

picks.name: Cafe Organic
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Cafe Organic embodies the quintessential Bali healthy cafe aesthetic with its bright, bohemian decor and beautifully presented plant-based dishes. While not exclusively vegan, they offer an extensive and clearly marked vegan menu featuring gorgeous smoothie bowls, avocado toasts, and vibrant salads. It's a popular spot for breakfast and brunch with a chic, relaxed atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their signature smoothie bowls like the 'Acai Bowl' or 'Pitaya Bowl'.
picks.insiderTip: Grab a seat on their charming outdoor terrace for the best people-watching.
picks.redditQuote: "Cafe Organic is so pretty and their vegan options are delicious. The 'Unicorn' smoothie bowl is almost too beautiful to eat, but it's totally worth it. Great spot for brunch in Seminyak."

faq.question: Is it easy to find vegan food in Bali?
faq.answer: Yes, Bali is an incredibly vegan-friendly destination, often considered a global hub for plant-based cuisine. You'll find a vast array of vegan and vegetarian cafes, restaurants, and warungs (local eateries) across the island, especially in popular areas like Ubud, Canggu, and Seminyak. Many non-vegan establishments also offer clearly marked vegan options.

faq.question: What kind of vegan food can I expect in Bali?
faq.answer: Bali's vegan food scene is highly diverse. You can expect everything from traditional Indonesian dishes (like Nasi Goreng, Gado-Gado, and curries) made vegan, to international healthy bowls, raw food, gourmet plant-based fine dining, and even vegan comfort food like burgers and pizzas. The focus is often on fresh, local ingredients and creative preparations.

faq.question: Are vegan cafes in Bali expensive?
faq.answer: Generally, vegan cafes in Bali are very affordable compared to Western prices. While high-end establishments exist, you can easily find delicious and filling vegan meals for IDR 60,000-150,000 (approximately $4-10 USD). Budget-friendly local warungs often offer vegan options for even less, making it accessible for all budgets.

faq.question: Do I need to make reservations for vegan cafes in Bali?
faq.answer: For most casual vegan cafes, reservations are not typically necessary, especially for breakfast or lunch. However, for more popular spots during peak meal times (e.g., brunch on weekends, dinner), or for higher-end vegan restaurants, it's always a good idea to book ahead, especially if you have a larger group or specific seating preference.

faq.question: Are there vegan cooking classes available in Bali?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Given Bali's thriving vegan scene, many cafes and culinary schools offer plant-based cooking classes. These are a fantastic way to learn how to prepare traditional Indonesian dishes with vegan ingredients or explore raw food techniques. Places like Moksa and Sayuri Healing Food often host workshops.

faq.question: What are some must-try vegan ingredients or dishes unique to Bali?
faq.answer: Don't miss dishes featuring tempeh and tofu, which are staples in Balinese cuisine and incredibly versatile. Also look for vegan rendang (often made with jackfruit), Nasi Campur (mixed rice with various sides), and smoothie bowls made with exotic local fruits like dragon fruit, mango, and mangosteen. Bali also offers an abundance of fresh, organic produce.

methodology: Our selection for Bali's best vegan cafes is curated from extensive research, incorporating local expert recommendations, aggregated online reviews, and personal visits. We prioritize venues offering diverse menus, high-quality ingredients, unique atmospheres, and consistent positive feedback to ensure a comprehensive and trustworthy guide.
